description: Opens the Godot editor on a project, or restarts or closes the one already connected, or binds its debug adapter again. close saves open scenes, quits the editor and waits for its process to go, which is the only way to end a hidden one short of killing it; an editor this server opened that has not connected yet has nothing of this server's to save, so close stops its process instead. open answers once the process has started, and the editor dials in after its import; a call needing the editor made before then waits for the one this server opened, for as long as a restart waits, and is refused naming it if it has not arrived. open refuses while an editor of the project is already running and has not reached this server, naming its pid, rather than putting a second on the project. The editor is an ordinary visible one on the desktop in use, and on Windows it is shown without being activated, so opening or reopening it does not take the keyboard from whatever the user is typing in. hidden: true opens it headless instead and, on Windows, on a desktop of its own, where the games it plays go too; a hidden editor serves the bridge, the language server and the debug adapter as a visible one does. A game a visible editor plays opens as a window on the desktop in use. An editor goes on serving the addon it read at startup, so restart is what puts a gdharness upgrade into effect, and nothing else here restarts one; it saves open scenes on the way out. An editor a server opened is started again by the server, hidden or visible and silent or not as it was started unless hidden or silent says otherwise, once the old one has gone: it waits 90 seconds for that, or GDHARNESS_EDITOR_RESTART_TIMEOUT_MS, and an old editor still running after it is not replaced, since the new one would find its ports held. One opened by hand restarts itself, which only one with a window can do, because the engine hands back none of the arguments it was started with. Godot tries each server port once, as the editor starts, so a restart binds a debug adapter that came back without its port again, in the editor that came back. rebind does the same for the connected editor without restarting it, whoever opened it; a debug session open on the adapter ends with it and is opened again by the next debug call. editor_status says which editor is connected and whether it is holding an old addon. Opening a project is a save and so is closing one, which is the part that is not obvious from outside: the editor imports the project on open and writes project.godot back, and Godot writes only what differs from its own defaults, so a key named deliberately at its default value is dropped either way. A restart of an editor this server opened is a quit and then a launch, and this server can be ended between them, usually by the reconnect the restart was being taken for: the editor is gone and nothing replaces it. That is written down before the quit, so the next server says so in editor_status rather than waiting for an editor that is not coming, and open finishes it. An open is refused when the editor it would start could never reach this server: a project other than the one this server serves, whose editor dials that project's own server; a project without the gdharness editor addon installed and enabled; and a project whose editor a restart is already bringing back. Operations: open (needs projectPath): open the editor on a project; restart: restart the connected editor and wait for it; close: save and quit the connected editor, and wait for it to go; rebind: stop and start the connected editor's debug adapter in place, ending its debug sessions, and answer whether it listens. Default open. The tool reference in the gdharness skill, and the site, say what every field of the answer means.

hidden.description: Open the editor headless and, on Windows, on a desktop of its own, so no window of it or of the games it plays appears. Default false on open: one visible editor, shown without taking the focus. On restart only for an editor a server opened, where the default is how the editor being replaced was started, read from its process; one whose start cannot be read is left running and refused until hidden is passed. One opened by hand comes back as it was, so hidden is refused there. Only for ops open, restart.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot. Only for op open.

silent.description: Open the editor with no sound out of the machine, started with --audio-driver Dummy, so a tool script, a preview or a scene playing in its viewport is heard by nobody. Default true on open, and on restart how the editor being replaced was started: pass false to hear it. The answer's arguments are what the editor was started with. The editor hands no audio driver to a game it plays, so editor_run's own silent decides that game's sound. A hidden editor is headless and silent either way. On restart only for an editor a server opened; one opened by hand comes back as it was. Only for ops open, restart.

name: editor_launch
title: Open, restart or close the editor, or bind its debug adapter again
